sentences.zh: 希望大家锁定收看。

sentences.en: Um, okay, so I'm going to record going on my morning run.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好的，我要记录一下我的晨跑过程。

sentences.en: It's 645, so here we go.
sentences.zh: 现在是6点45分，我们出发吧。

sentences.en: So, keys, mask, phone, we're out.
sentences.zh: 钥匙、口罩、手机，我们出门。

sentences.en: I run.
sentences.zh: 我跑步。

sentences.en: I run a lot.
sentences.zh: 我跑得很多。

sentences.en: I run by myself.
sentences.zh: 我一个人跑。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I find running to be actually quite meditative.
sentences.zh: 我发现跑步其实是一件非常具有冥想性质的事情。

sentences.en: And what I am thinking about, usually I'm thinking about my day.
sentences.zh: 而我通常在想的，是我这一天的事情。

sentences.en: And recently, I'm thinking a lot about the people who have come before me.
sentences.zh: 最近，我经常想起那些在我之前走过这条路的人。

sentences.en: I'm thinking a lot about the lessons my grandparents taught me without actually saying anything.
sentences.zh: 我经常想起我的祖父母在什么都没说的情况下教给我的那些道理。

sentences.en: Namely, that if the people you love, and I love Black people, need something, and you've got it, you have to share it.
sentences.zh: 也就是，如果你爱的人——我爱黑人同胞——需要什么，而你刚好有，你就必须分享出来。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: As protests against police brutality enter their third month, meaningful reform remains elusive.
sentences.zh: 随着抗议警察暴力的活动进入第三个月，有意义的改革依然遥不可及。

sentences.en: My colleague, Caitlin Dickerson, spoke with one demonstrator about her journey to the front lines and the lessons she's learned about the pace of change.
sentences.zh: 我的同事凯特琳·迪克森采访了一位示威者，听她讲述自己走上抗议前线的历程，以及她对变革步伐的感悟。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 5th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月5日，星期三。

sentences.en: So, let's jump in.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们切入正题。

sentences.en: And I think starting at the beginning would be great.
sentences.zh: 我想从头讲起会很好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, my name is Sharonda Bossier.
sentences.zh: 我叫夏龙达·博西尔。

sentences.en: I grew up in the Watts section of Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 我在洛杉矶的沃茨区长大。

sentences.en: And I was raised by my grandparents because my mother struggled with addiction and could not raise us.
sentences.zh: 我由祖父母抚养长大，因为我母亲饱受毒瘾困扰，无法抚养我们。

sentences.en: And my father was incarcerated.
sentences.zh: 而我的父亲则身陷囹圄。

sentences.en: So, Sharonda Bossier is born in 1984.
sentences.zh: 所以，夏龙达·博西尔出生于1984年。

sentences.en: And she grows up in the care of her grandparents, who moved to Los Angeles, both from Louisiana during the Great
sentences.zh: 她在祖父母的照顾下长大，她的祖父母都是在大迁徙时期从路易斯安那州搬到洛杉矶的。

sentences.en: Migration.
sentences.zh: 迁徙。

sentences.en: It's a household that is really kind of steeped in the past, steeped in music.
sentences.zh: 这是一个深深沉浸在过去、沉浸在音乐中的家庭。

sentences.en: My grandfather was a pretty big James Brown fan.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父是詹姆斯·布朗的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: My grandfather loved Sam Cooke.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父非常喜欢萨姆·库克。

sentences.en: And so, themes around race were pretty present in the music they played.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们播放的音乐中经常出现关于种族的主题。

sentences.en: There's a Sam Cooke song called Last Mile of the Way.
sentences.zh: 有一首萨姆·库克的歌叫《最后一英里》。

sentences.en: It's a gospel song.
sentences.zh: 这是一首福音歌曲。

sentences.en: But one of the things that I remember talking to my grandfather about was work and how the song talked about work and physical labor.
sentences.zh: 但我记得和祖父谈论过的一件事是关于工作，以及这首歌如何歌唱工作和体力劳动。

sentences.en: And as a sort of metaphor for kind of getting to heaven.
sentences.zh: 并以此作为通往天堂的一种隐喻。

sentences.en: And how just angry he was about that being the only promise for safety and reward we had as Black people.
sentences.zh: 以及他对这种事感到多么愤怒，因为这是我们作为黑人所拥有的唯一的安全和回报的承诺。

sentences.en: What were you like as a kid?
sentences.zh: 你小时候是什么样的孩子？

sentences.en: I think it really depends on who you ask.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的取决于你问的是谁。

sentences.en: I was always a really good student.
sentences.zh: 我一直是个非常好的学生。

sentences.en: I always earned really good grades.
sentences.zh: 我的成绩总是非常好。

sentences.en: I was always at the top of my class.
sentences.zh: 我总是名列前茅。

sentences.en: My grandparents said there were two things we always had to do in our house, and that was go to school and go to church.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父母说，我们家有两件事是必须做的，那就是上学和去教堂。

sentences.en: But I have always had sort of a knack, I guess you could say, for challenging authority,
sentences.zh: 但我一直有一种天赋，你可以这么说，那就是挑战权威，

sentences.en: always asking why about the things I see around me.
sentences.zh: 总是对周围看到的事情刨根问底。

sentences.en: And so, I really credit my grandmother and, you know, her standing behind me and saying to me, like, if you have questions, you should ask them.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很感谢我的祖母，你知道的，她站在我身后对我说，如果你有问题，就应该去问。

sentences.en: And if a person in authority tries to sort of, you know, push back or squash that in you, I got your back.
sentences.zh: 如果权威人士试图，你知道的，反击或试图压制你的这种精神，我永远支持你。

sentences.en: And that mattered to me tremendously as a young person.
sentences.zh: 这对我年轻时的成长有着极其重要的意义。

sentences.en: I think that she wished that she had asked why more.
sentences.zh: 我想她一定希望自己当年能多问几个为什么。

sentences.en: I think she realized that she likely would have made a different set of decisions had she questioned what was expected of a poor Black girl born in 1932 in New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 我想她意识到，如果她当初去质疑那些对一个1932年出生在新奥尔良的贫苦黑人女孩的期待，她可能会做出不同的人生选择。

sentences.en: Sharonda is very close to her grandmother, and her grandmother works hard basically to shape Sharonda
sentences.zh: 夏龙达和祖母非常亲近，祖母努力工作，基本上把夏龙达塑造成为一个

sentences.en: into this young woman who knows her history, understands what her family's been through,
sentences.zh: 了解自己历史、明白家人经历过什么、祖先经历过什么的年轻女性，

sentences.en: what her ancestors have been through, and also to feel free to build the life that she wants.
sentences.zh: 同时也让她能够自由地去构建自己想要的生活。

sentences.en: My grandmother told me that I only have to do two things in this life, and that's stay Black and die,
sentences.zh: 我祖母告诉我，在这个世界上我只需做好两件事，那就是保持黑人本色并走向死亡，

sentences.en: and that it was my life, and it was mine to live as I chose.
sentences.zh: 这是我的人生，要由我自己选择怎么过。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Her saying stay Black and die is saying those two things are going to happen, and anything else is really up to you.
sentences.zh: 她说保持黑人本色并走向死亡，意思是这两件事是注定会发生的，而除此之外的一切真的都取决于你。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So how do these teachings inform Sharonda's view of this neighborhood around her, Watts?
sentences.zh: 那么这些教导是如何影响夏龙达对她周围这个社区——沃茨的看法的？

sentences.en: You know, she remembers a community with a lot of police, but not a whole lot of protection.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她记忆中的社区有许多警察，却没有多少保护。

sentences.en: This is sort of the height of the war on drugs and the war against gangs.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是向毒品战争和帮派战争宣战的最高峰时期。

sentences.en: So I see police everywhere,
sentences.zh: 所以我到处都能看到警察，

sentences.en: and yet there are regular and consistent drive-by shootings.
sentences.zh: 然而车内枪击事件却依然频发。

sentences.en: I see police pulling people over.
sentences.zh: 我看到警察拦下路人。

sentences.en: I see men thrown up against walls.
sentences.zh: 我看到男人被推向墙壁。

sentences.en: Mostly those are the images that stick with me.
sentences.zh: 这些基本上是我脑海中最深刻的画面。

sentences.en: And still, I know people whose homes have been robbed.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，我还是认识有人家里遭了强盗。

sentences.en: And so I'm like, the police are everywhere, and yet the crime that harms us still happens?
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，警察到处都是，为什么伤害我们的犯罪行为还是会发生？

sentences.en: How is that?
sentences.zh: 怎么会这样？

sentences.en: Her grandparents taught her very early on, basically that the police were not her friends.
sentences.zh: 她的祖父母很早就教导她，基本上警察并不是她的朋友。

sentences.en: And the message that she got was actually that her grandparents were there to protect her from the police.
sentences.zh: 她得到的讯息实际上是，她的祖父母是为了保护她免受警察的伤害。

sentences.en: So as a kid, she internalizes this message of caution, and it comes out in interactions with the police, but that's not the only way it comes out.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个孩子，她内化了这种警惕的信息，它会在与警察的互动中表现出来，但这并不是唯一的表现方式。

sentences.en: For example, one Sunday, after church, she's walking with her grandmother to this meat market that they used to go to all the
sentences.zh: 比如，有一个星期天，做完礼拜后，她和祖母一起走向他们经常去的一家肉铺，

sentences.en: time because it was kind of on the other side of town, but it was near their church.
sentences.zh: 因为那家店在镇子的另一头，但离他们的教堂很近。

sentences.en: So they would always stop there on the way home.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在回家的路上总是会顺便去那里。

sentences.en: And her grandmother would be humming the music that they'd heard in church that day.
sentences.zh: 她的祖母会哼唱他们在那天教堂里听到的音乐。

sentences.en: But she was at the meat counter, and I sort of wandered off, as kids do.
sentences.zh: 但当时她在肉柜台前，而我像小孩子一样到处乱跑。

sentences.en: And I remember a man had come from behind the meat counter to say to me, you better go back with your mom.
sentences.zh: 我记得有个男人从肉柜台后面走出来对我说，你最好回到你妈妈身边去。

sentences.en: And there was something about his tone that immediately sort of shifted when I said, that's not my mom.
sentences.zh: 当我回答说“那不是我妈妈”时，他的语气立刻发生了某种微妙的变化。

sentences.en: He was not expecting a kid to talk back to him, number one, and I think especially not a Black kid to talk back to him.
sentences.zh: 第一，他没想到一个小孩会顶嘴，而且我觉得他尤其没想到一个黑人小孩会顶嘴。

sentences.en: And it's very clear that he's upset about this whole situation.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他对整个情况感到很不高兴。

sentences.en: There's just this tension that makes her a little nervous.
sentences.zh: 这种紧张气氛让夏龙达感到有些紧张。

sentences.en: And I could tell as we walked away that my grandmother actually was a little shaken by it.
sentences.zh: 我能看出当我们走开时，我的祖母其实也为此感到有些震惊。

sentences.en: I didn't know why.
sentences.zh: 我当时不知道为什么。

sentences.en: I didn't have the language to say why, but I never wandered off again.
sentences.zh: 我没有语言来表达原因，但我再也没有到处乱跑过。

sentences.en: That day eventually makes a lot more sense to Sharonda a few years later because of something that happens in her community.
sentences.zh: 几年后，因为社区里发生的一件事，那天的经历对夏龙达来说终于变得更加明了。

sentences.en: The girl was killed over a bottle of orange juice.
sentences.zh: 这个女孩因一瓶橙汁而被杀。

sentences.en: Over a bottle of orange juice.
sentences.zh: 仅仅为了一瓶橙汁。

sentences.en: Store owner Soon-Jadu thought 15-year-old Latasha Harlins was going to steal some orange juice.
sentences.zh: 店主顺珠认为15岁的拉塔莎·哈林斯想要偷橙汁。

sentences.en: Latasha Harlins, who is a 15-year-old teenager in 1991 when she walks into a grocery store in South
sentences.zh: 拉塔莎·哈林斯，1991年时她是一名15岁的少年，当时她走进了南洛杉矶的一家杂货店。

sentences.en: Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶。

sentences.en: And she picks up a bottle of orange juice worth $1.79.
sentences.zh: 她拿起了一瓶价值1.79美元的橙汁。

sentences.en: And people who are in the store say that Latasha puts the orange juice in her backpack and she has $2 in her hand.
sentences.zh: 店里的人说，拉塔莎把橙汁放进背包里，手里拿着2美元。

sentences.en: And she's walking toward the counter when the store owner grabs Latasha's sweater.
sentences.zh: 正当她走向柜台时，店主抓住了拉塔莎的毛衣。

sentences.en: And Latasha punches her in the face.
sentences.zh: 拉塔莎打了她的脸。

sentences.en: And she puts the orange juice on the counter and she heads for the door.
sentences.zh: 她把橙汁放在柜台上，然后朝门口走去。

sentences.en: And the store owner picks up a handgun and shoots her in the back of the head, killing her instantly.
sentences.zh: 店主拿起一把手枪朝她的后脑勺开枪，当场将她击毙。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: The store owner accused Harlins of stealing the juice.
sentences.zh: 店主指控哈林斯偷了果汁。

sentences.en: There was a confrontation And she sees why her grandmother was so nervous for her that day in the store.
sentences.zh: 双方发生了冲突，她终于明白为什么那天在店里祖母会为她感到那么紧张。

sentences.en: I think it was an injustice.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一场不公。

sentences.en: Justice has not been served.
sentences.zh: 正义并未得到伸张。

sentences.en: This lady has killed my 15-year-old granddaughter.
sentences.zh: 这个女人杀了我15岁的孙女。

sentences.en: And she'll get away with five years probation.
sentences.zh: 而她却只判了五年缓刑就逃脱了法律制裁。

sentences.en: This is an injustice.
sentences.zh: 这太不公平了。

sentences.en: Get the camera out of my face.
sentences.zh: 把镜头从我脸上拿开。

sentences.en: Move!
sentences.zh: 走开！

sentences.en: It's right around this time that a video surfaces.
sentences.zh: 就在这个时候，一段视频浮出水面。

sentences.en: In Los Angeles, outrage grows over a videotape of police beating an unarmed motoriSt.
sentences.zh: 在洛杉矶，一段警察殴打无辜司机的录像引发了巨大的愤怒。

sentences.en: Of Rodney King being brutally beaten by police.
sentences.zh: 罗德尼·金遭到警察残酷殴打的事件。

sentences.en: A case involving white police officers.
sentences.zh: 这是一起涉及白人警察的案件。

sentences.en: Beating a man they had just pulled over.
sentences.zh: 殴打了一个他们刚刚拦下的男子。

sentences.en: And an amateur cameraman recorded it all.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都被一名业余摄像师记录了下来。

sentences.en: The incident really takes over Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 这起事件彻底震动了洛杉矶。

sentences.en: It takes over Watts, where Sharonda lives.
sentences.zh: 它震动了夏龙达居住的沃茨区。

sentences.en: For some reason, her grandparents had TVs in almost every room in the house.
sentences.zh: 不知为什么，她的祖父母几乎每个房间都放了电视机。

sentences.en: And they were just blaring day and night.
sentences.zh: 而且它们日夜大声播放着。

sentences.en: I had to come here and let my voice be heard.
sentences.zh: 我必须来这里发出我的声音。

sentences.en: Where are these people from?
sentences.zh: 这些人是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: And I remember, you know, my grandparents hosted a regular Spades game, right, where my aunts and uncles and cousins would come by.
sentences.zh: 我记得，你知道的，我的祖父母经常组织玩黑桃牌游戏，我的阿姨、叔叔和表亲们都会来。

sentences.en: And I remember just hearing at the card table conversations about and debates about, you know, what they thought would happen.
sentences.zh: 我记得在牌桌上听到大家关于他们认为会发生什么的对话和辩论。

sentences.en: Who they thought would actually be convicted of anything.
sentences.zh: 关于他们认为谁会被真正定罪。

sentences.en: One of my uncles, I remember just, he, he was fiery.
sentences.zh: 我记得我的一位叔叔，他当时脾气很火爆。

sentences.en: Um, but in this moment, he just sort of was like, man, we know ain't nothing gonna happen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但在那个时刻，他只是觉得，天哪，我们知道什么都不会发生。

sentences.en: Like, we might as well just play cards.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们还不如直接打牌呢。

sentences.en: And that just did not make sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我完全无法理解。

sentences.en: And I did not understand why my uncle thought that.
sentences.zh: 我不明白为什么我叔叔会这么想。

sentences.en: Because my seven-year-old brain was like, they did something wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为我七岁的大脑觉得，他们做错了事。

sentences.en: They will be punished, right?
sentences.zh: 他们会受到惩罚，对吧？

sentences.en: And my seven-year-old brain didn't understand
sentences.zh: 而我七岁的大脑并不明白

sentences.en: that that's not how things work here.
sentences.zh: 事情在这里并不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: Like, he knew something that she didn't, couldn't possibly, given her age.
sentences.zh: 我的叔叔知道一些她不知道的事情，以她的年龄根本不可能知道。

sentences.en: He understood a kind of different form of gravity in the universe.
sentences.zh: 他理解宇宙中另一种不同形式的引力。

sentences.en: That's a good way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 这个比喻真好。

sentences.en: There was a different force like gravity, something else that she hadn't learned about in school that she wasn't familiar with yet, but that was
sentences.zh: 有一种不同的力量就像重力一样，是她以前在学校里没学过、也还不熟悉的东西，但这将会冲击到她生命中迄今为止所接受的教育中

sentences.en: going to impact this, you know, trajectory or natural order of things that she had been taught so far in her life.
sentences.zh: 那种轨迹或事物自然秩序。

sentences.en: Here outside Parker Center, where protesters have descended on the place, it was-
sentences.zh: 这里是帕克中心外，抗议者们蜂拥而至，当时——

sentences.en: One question on everyone's mind is how did this jury see the same videotape that the world saw and reached the conclusion that no crime was being committed?
sentences.zh: 每个人心里都有一个疑问，为什么这个陪审团看到的录像带和全世界看到的一样，却得出了没有犯罪的结论？

sentences.en: All of a sudden, I flipped the channel and here's a non-guilty, non-guilty.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我换了台，然后就看到无罪，无罪。

sentences.en: I started crying.
sentences.zh: 我开始哭了。

sentences.en: I mean, that really, that hurt because it was- We are Rodney King's peers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的，这很伤人，因为——我们是罗德尼·金的同龄人。

sentences.en: We are Eula Mae Love's peers.
sentences.zh: 我们是尤拉·梅·洛夫的同龄人。

sentences.en: We are Latasha Harlan's peers.
sentences.zh: 我们是拉塔莎·哈兰斯的同龄人。

sentences.en: Not that jury.
sentences.zh: 但那个陪审团不是。

sentences.en: And then I remember going back to church and going back to school
sentences.zh: 然后我记得回到教堂，回到学校

sentences.en: and just not talking about it.
sentences.zh: 却绝口不提这件事。

sentences.en: But all around me, I could see the burned buildings, right?
sentences.zh: 但在我周围，我能看到被烧毁的建筑，对吧？

sentences.en: Like the pep boys wasn't there anymore, right?
sentences.zh: 就像Pep Boys汽车用品店不在了，对吧？

sentences.en: The supermarket wasn't there anymore.
sentences.zh: 那个超市也不在了。

sentences.en: And we just didn't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 而我们就是不谈论它。

sentences.en: So Sharonda and her family go back to normal, kind of as if nothing ever happened until a few years later when their whole lives are upended.
sentences.zh: 所以沙龙达和她的家人恢复了正常生活，好像什么都没发生过一样，直到几年后，他们的整个生活被彻底颠覆。

sentences.en: So I'm 13 and I come home after my babysitting job.
sentences.zh: 所以我13岁时，做完保姆工作回到家。

sentences.en: It's about nine o'clock, right?
sentences.zh: 大约九点钟，对吧？

sentences.en: Not too late.
sentences.zh: 不算太晚。

sentences.en: And I have a late dinner by myself.
sentences.zh: 我一个人吃了顿晚饭。

sentences.en: My grandmother is in her room, you know, probably watching either In the Heat of the Night or Matlock.
sentences.zh: 我外祖母在她的房间里，你知道的，大概在看《炎热的午夜》或者《梅特洛克》。

sentences.en: And we chat for a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了一会儿。

sentences.en: I say, good night.
sentences.zh: 我说，晚安。

sentences.en: I love you.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。

sentences.en: I give her a kiss, right?
sentences.zh: 我吻了她一下，对吧？

sentences.en: I head to bed.
sentences.zh: 我上床睡觉了。

sentences.en: And in the middle of the night, I wake up because my grandfather is screaming my name and saying, call 9-1-1, call 9-1-1.
sentences.zh: 半夜里，我醒了过来，因为我外祖父在大声喊我的名字，说，快打911，快打911。

sentences.en: And my grandmother is having a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 我外祖母心脏病发作了。

sentences.en: Her grandmother is taken to Martin Luther King
sentences.zh: 她的外祖母被送到马丁·路德·金

sentences.en: Hospital.
sentences.zh: 医院。

sentences.en: It's a public hospital.
sentences.zh: 那是一家公立医院。

sentences.en: And it's known in the community as Killer King, known for not providing good care.
sentences.zh: 在社区里它被称为“杀手金”，以医疗服务质量差而闻名。

sentences.en: And when the doctor, a white man, walked in, my sister and I just started wailing.
sentences.zh: 当那个白人医生走进来时，我和妹妹顿时放声大哭。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: We knew that doctors didn't make time for you unless things were really bad.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，除非情况真的很糟糕，否则医生是不会为你抽出时间的。

sentences.en: Um, and we just sort of knew.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们心里其实都有数。

sentences.en: And for Sharonda, she's really taking note of the conversations around her.
sentences.zh: 对于沙龙达来说，她把周围人的谈话都记在了心里。

sentences.en: We have a funeral and people are at the house and, you know, aunts and uncles and church
sentences.zh: 我们办了葬礼，家里聚满了人，你知道的，阿姨、叔叔和教堂

sentences.en: members come by and, you know, you hear over and over again, well, why'd they take her to King?
sentences.zh: 成员都来了，你知道的，你反复听到有人说，唉，他们为什么要送她去金医院？

sentences.en: Or, oh, Lord, she went to King?
sentences.zh: 或者，哦，天哪，她去了金医院？

sentences.en: And there was just this sense that, you know, maybe things could have been different if she had gone somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 当时就是有一种感觉，你知道的，如果她去了别的地方，事情也许就会不一样了。

sentences.en: And you just, you'll never know.
sentences.zh: 而你就是，你永远不会知道了。

sentences.en: And so she becomes a really angry kid.
sentences.zh: 所以她成了一个非常愤怒的孩子。

sentences.en: I was pretty angry at God when my grandmother died.
sentences.zh: 外祖母去世时，我对上帝相当愤怒。

sentences.en: Um, I felt like I had been dealt a pretty shorthand already on the parent front.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得在父母方面，命运已经给了一手很烂的牌。

sentences.en: Parents who struggled with addiction, a father who was incarcerated, a mother who was absent for most of my life.
sentences.zh: 与毒瘾挣扎的父母，身陷囹圄的父亲，在我生命大部分时间里缺席的母亲。

sentences.en: And then to take the only mother I had ever known at 13, I just, I didn't know what kind of God would do that.
sentences.zh: 然后在13岁时夺走了我唯一知道的母亲，我只是，我不知道什么样的上帝会做出这种事。

sentences.en: So I enter high school just mad at the world and mad at authority in particular.
sentences.zh: 所以我进入高中时，对整个世界充满愤怒，尤其是对权威充满愤怒。

sentences.en: She gets in a lot of fights, a lot of fights, but there are a couple of teachers who she gets along
sentences.zh: 她经常打架，打了很多次架，但有几个老师她跟他们

sentences.en: with really well, who seem to understand what she's going through, see it for what it is.
sentences.zh: 相处得非常好，他们似乎理解她正在经历什么，并看清了事情的本质。

sentences.en: And they're pretty determined to help her through it.
sentences.zh: 他们决心帮她度过难关。

sentences.en: So there's one teacher in particular, her English teacher, Mrs. Campbell.
sentences.zh: 所以特别是有一位老师，她的英语老师，坎贝尔太太。

sentences.en: And she says to Sharonda, you know, you could really do something with all this anger that you're feeling.
sentences.zh: 她对沙龙达说，你知道的，你可以把感受到的这些愤怒做点有意义的事。

sentences.en: And Sharonda's like, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 沙龙达就问，您是什么意思？

sentences.en: I thought initially that my teachers were going to have me do something whack, like a petition drive or join student government.
sentences.zh: 我最初以为我的老师会让我做一些很无聊的事，比如发起请愿或加入学生会。

sentences.en: And I had no interest in doing that.
sentences.zh: 我对这些毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: And Mrs. Campbell says, you can protest, you can try to change these things that you don't think are fair.
sentences.zh: 坎贝尔太太说，你可以抗议，你可以试着改变那些你认为不公平的事情。

sentences.en: You can become an activiSt. And what did Sharonda make of that?
sentences.zh: 你可以成为一名活动家。沙龙达对此作何感想？

sentences.en: It really resonates with her.
sentences.zh: 这在她的内心产生了强烈共鸣。

sentences.en: And she decides to participate in a school walkout for the first time.
sentences.zh: 她决定第一次参加学校的罢课抗议。

sentences.en: And it's one that's being organized because some of her peers were upset that they were attending a school called George Washington High that was named after a slave owner.
sentences.zh: 这次罢课是由一些同学组织起来的，因为他们对就读于一所名叫乔治·华盛顿高中的学校感到不满，而这所学校是以一个奴隶主的名字命名的。

sentences.en: And on the day of the walkout, you know, she remembers pausing before she reached the doors of the school, looking around.
sentences.zh: 在罢课那天，你知道的，她记得在走到学校大门前时停顿了一下，环顾四周。

sentences.en: And I remember security guards standing at the gates and saying, if you walk out, we're going to report your name to the front office.
sentences.zh: 我记得保安站在大门口说，如果你走出去，我们会把你的名字报给前台办公室。

sentences.en: And she just takes this deep breath, like, am I doing this?
sentences.zh: 她只是深深吸了一口气，心想，我真的要这么做吗？

sentences.en: If I had to call my grandfather and say, grandpa, I'm at the police station because I walked out of school.
sentences.zh: 如果我不得不打电话给外祖父说，爷爷，我在警察局，因为我从学校罢课走了出来。

sentences.en: I, I, I couldn't imagine having to do that.
sentences.zh: 我，我，我简直无法想象自己不得不这样做。

sentences.en: And then exhales and decides she's doing this.
sentences.zh: 接着她呼出一口气，决定豁出去了。

sentences.en: I got to walk out.
sentences.zh: 我必须走出去。

sentences.en: So she blows past the security guard out the doors.
sentences.zh: 于是她从保安身旁冲了过去，冲出大门。

sentences.en: She remembers feeling, you know, the fresh air on her skin and just feeling a release, a release that feels productive.
sentences.zh: 她记得感觉到，你知道的，新鲜空气吹在皮肤上，并感觉到一种释放，一种富有成效的释放。

sentences.en: I think I was setting out to prove to myself and to others that as the kids say now, I was about this life, right?
sentences.zh: 我想我当时是在向自己和他人证明，正如现在的孩子们所说，我是玩真的，对吧？

sentences.en: That I could work up the courage to stand up to authority in a way that could result in real consequences for me.
sentences.zh: 我能鼓起勇气以一种可能会给我带来真正后果的方式对抗权威。

sentences.en: It's my life and I get to do with it what I want.
sentences.zh: 这是我的人生，我想怎么过就怎么过。

sentences.en: But, you know, Sharonda's been taught from childhood that there are two inevitable realities in life and the rest is really up to her.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，沙龙达从小就被教导，生活中存在两个不可避免的现实，剩下的其实全靠她自己决定。

sentences.en: And this is the first moment of her starting to figure out what does she want to do in between?
sentences.zh: 这是她开始摸索自己究竟想在中间做些什么的第一刻。

sentences.en: Um, as you can imagine, that, that, that meant sometimes that I was going to decide against my grandfather's wishes to walk out of school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所想象的那样，那，那，那意味着有时我会违背外祖父的意愿选择罢课。

sentences.en: Um, he wasn't always thrilled about that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他对那事可不总是兴高采烈。

sentences.en: But yeah, I, I was very clear that I got to do what I wanted.
sentences.zh: 但没错，我，我很清楚我得做自己想做的事。

sentences.en: And once she figures that out, the next few years really kind of fall into place for Sharonda.
sentences.zh: 一旦她明白了这一点，接下来的几年对沙龙达来说就都顺理成章了。

sentences.en: So she continues to participate in protests over not just the name of her school, but the amount of funding that it gets from the city, the very low graduation rates that it has.
sentences.zh: 于是她继续参加抗议活动，抗议的内容不仅是学校的名字，还包括它从市政府获得的资金数额，以及它非常低的毕业率。

sentences.en: And that evolves naturally into her after graduating college, deciding to become a teacher herself to try to address some of these inequities that she saw when she was growing up.
sentences.zh: 这很自然地演变成她在大学毕业后，决定自己成为一名教师，试图解决她成长时期看到的这些不平等现象。

sentences.en: And around the same time, Barack Obama campaigns for president, which is this really kind of electric moment for young black professionals.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，贝拉克·奥巴马竞选总统，对于年轻的黑人专业人士来说，这真是一个极具感染力的时刻。

sentences.en: Look at all of you.
sentences.zh: 看看你们所有人。

sentences.en: So for the first time in a long time, you had an entire generation of young people and young
sentences.zh: 所以在很长一段时间里，你第一次看到整整一代年轻人和刚刚

sentences.en: professionals who were just out of college in their first jobs and got picked up by the Obama machine.
sentences.zh: 大学毕业参加第一份工作的年轻专业人士被奥巴马的竞选机器吸纳了进去。

sentences.en: And she volunteers for the campaign and she meets a lot of other like-minded organizers.
sentences.zh: 她为竞选活动做志愿者，并遇到了许多其他志同道合的组织者。

sentences.en: You're young, you're black, you're a professional, you just kind of know each other.
sentences.zh: 你年轻，你是黑人，你是专业人士，你们自然而然就互相认识了。

sentences.en: And work with you today, together, we can finish the work that needs to be done and usher in a new birth of freedom on this earth.
sentences.zh: 今天与你们并肩作战，我们可以完成需要完成的工作，在这片土地上开启自由的新生。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, everybody.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: And then something happens that really changes the trajectory of Sharonda's life.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件事，彻底改变了沙龙达的生活轨迹。

sentences.en: Actually, two things happen that change the trajectory of where she's headed.
sentences.zh: 实际上，发生了两件事，改变了她前进的方向。

sentences.en: She's living in New York City, working in education when Trayvon Martin is killed in Florida.
sentences.zh: 当特雷沃恩·马丁在佛罗里达州被杀时，她正住在纽约市从事教育工作。

sentences.en: And so we begin to show up to marches and we begin to show up to protests.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始出现在游行队伍中，我们开始出现在抗议活动中。

sentences.en: And I think one of the things that is beautiful about this particular moment is that there is this sense that any one of us can put out a call to action and someone will show up.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个特殊时刻美妙的地方在于，有一种感觉，我们中的任何一个人都可以发出行动呼吁，就会有人响应。

sentences.en: And that idea begins to gain traction over the next year until August 9th, 2014.
sentences.zh: 这个想法在接下来的一年里开始受到关注，直到2014年8月9日。

sentences.en: What are they saying to you, the police, what are they saying to you right now about what's happened to your son?
sentences.zh: 他们对你说了什么，警察，他们现在对你说了关于你儿子发生了什么的事吗？

sentences.en: They aren't telling me anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么都没告诉我。

sentences.en: They haven't told me anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么都没告诉我。

sentences.en: They wouldn't even let me identify my son.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不让我去辨认我儿子的尸体。

sentences.en: When Michael Brown Jr., who's 18 years old, is fatally shot by a white police officer in Ferguson, Missouri.
sentences.zh: 当时18岁的迈克尔·布朗在密苏里州弗格森被一名白人警察开枪击毙。

sentences.en: ...on that phone and say, yeah, that's my son.
sentences.zh: ……对着那个电话说，是的，那是我的儿子。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 我非常难过。

sentences.en: Laying in the street for hours.
sentences.zh: 倒在街上好几个小时。

sentences.en: Hours.
sentences.zh: 好几个小时。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 我非常难过。

sentences.en: And then it erupts.
sentences.zh: 然后冲突爆发了。

sentences.en: Street violence raged for hours last night.
sentences.zh: 昨晚街头暴力持续了数小时。

sentences.en: At least two people in a crowd of protesters were shot.
sentences.zh: 抗议人群中至少有两人遭枪击。

sentences.en: And all of this started just hours after National Guard troops arrived in for...
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在国民警卫队部队抵达……后仅仅几个小时。

sentences.en: Community there, outraged after the fatal shooting death of an unarmed...
sentences.zh: 那里的社区对一名手无寸铁的……遭枪击身亡感到愤怒

sentences.en: We need justice for our son.
sentences.zh: 我们需要为我们的儿子伸张正义。

sentences.en: We need justice for our son.
sentences.zh: 我们需要为我们的儿子伸张正义。

sentences.en: It becomes Sharonda's focus in life, what she wants to try to change.
sentences.zh: 这成了沙龙达生活的重心，她想要努力改变的事情。

sentences.en: And so she just gets on that train and starts to become a part of the movement.
sentences.zh: 于是她直接上了那列火车，开始成为这场运动的一部分。

sentences.en: There's sort of an activist railroad.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是一个活动家的铁路网。

sentences.en: There are busloads of people who go from New York, right?
sentences.zh: 有满满一车又一车的人从纽约出发，对吧？

sentences.en: So we start raising money for that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始为此筹款。

sentences.en: There's the need for supplies to Ferguson.
sentences.zh: 弗格森有物资需求。

sentences.en: So we start raising money for that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始为此筹款。

sentences.en: You know, she's got a job, a nine-to-five job in New York, but she starts to dedicate all of her extra time to these issues.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她在纽约有一份朝九晚五的工作，但她开始把所有的业余时间都奉献给这些问题。

sentences.en: Her weekends are spent on the phone with people who are on the ground in Ferguson and in other cities where protests are breaking out.
sentences.zh: 她的周末都是在打电话中度过的，对象是在弗格森以及其他爆发抗议的城市实地声援的人们。

sentences.en: And she actually reconnects with people she met during President Obama's 2008 campaign.
sentences.zh: 她甚至重新联系了她在奥巴马2008年竞选期间认识的人。

sentences.en: Okay, what are you guys working on?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你们在搞什么？

sentences.en: What should we be working on?
sentences.zh: 我们应该在搞什么？

sentences.en: You know, what are your police allowed to do?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们的警察被允许做什么？

sentences.en: What's in their contract that shouldn't be in ours?
sentences.zh: 他们的合同里有什么是不应该在我们合同里的？

sentences.en: What's the difference between a chokehold and a stranglehold?
sentences.zh: 锁喉和扼颈有什么区别？

sentences.en: How do we talk about that?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何谈论这个？

sentences.en: So we start building these networks and these friendships that help us share information, that help us strategize.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始建立这些网络和友谊，帮助我们分享信息，帮助我们制定战略。

sentences.en: They don't really want to push for change within government, within a system that they fundamentally think is broken, don't believe in.
sentences.zh: 他们并不真正想在政府内部推动变革，他们从根本上认为这个体制已经破碎，并不相信它。

sentences.en: How you doing?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Are you here to support us?
sentences.zh: 你是来支持我们的吗？

sentences.en: You are?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Because we haven't seen you marching at all, Jesse.
sentences.zh: 因为我们根本没看到你在游行，杰西。

sentences.en: We ain't seen you.
sentences.zh: 我们没看到你。

sentences.en: When are you going to stop selling us out, Jesse?
sentences.zh: 你什么时候才停止出卖我们，杰西？

sentences.en: We don't want you here in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 我们不欢迎你来圣路易斯。

sentences.en: We activists out here, brother.
sentences.zh: 我们才是这里的活动家，兄弟。

sentences.en: This is real.
sentences.zh: 这是来真的。

sentences.en: We don't want you here.

sentences.zh: 你不是领袖。

sentences.zh: 我们不欢迎你在这里。

sentences.en: We were a grassroots, pretty leaderless, dispersed network of people, all guided by a sort of North Star, right?
sentences.zh: 我们是一个基层、基本上没有领袖、分散的人际网络，所有人都在某种北极星的指引下，对吧？

sentences.en: Which was hashtag Black Lives Matter.
sentences.zh: 那就是“黑人的命也是命”话题标签。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，每晚你都要带300张最珍贵的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 把DJ台变成一个美丽的、有50年历史的文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听奥彼（Audemars Piguet）的《The Reframers》。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用，即可享受首月免费体验。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用并获得30天的免费访问权。

sentences.en: What are these organizers hoping to achieve by not raising up a singular figure, by being kind of leaderless?
sentences.zh: 这些组织者不树立单一的领袖，采用某种去中心化的无领袖模式，是希望达到什么目的？

sentences.en: What Sharonda says is that, you know, at this point in her life,
sentences.zh: 夏龙达说的是，你知道的，在她人生的这个阶段，

sentences.en: she is feeling really suspicious of hierarchy, of any kind of concentration of power that disenfranchises people below.
sentences.zh: 她对等级制度感到非常怀疑，对任何剥夺底层人民权利的权力集中都感到怀疑。

sentences.en: But because they choose to avoid establishing leaders, it's really confusing and a turnoff to a lot of the country
sentences.zh: 但由于他们选择避免确立领导人，这让全国许多人感到非常困惑和反感，

sentences.en: who don't feel like they hear a clear message coming from one person and who are also noticing that some protests have turned violent and are really uncomfortable with that.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得听不到来自一个人的清晰声音，而且他们也注意到有些抗议活动已经演变成暴力，对此感到非常不安。

sentences.en: There's a way in which this movement becomes really big, but the support for it across the country also kind of hits a ceiling.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，这场运动变得规模庞大，但全国上下对它的支持也遇到了一种天花板。

sentences.en: It's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: The movement is suspicious of leaders and some of the public is suspicious of a movement without a leader.
sentences.zh: 这场运动对领导人持怀疑态度，而一部分公众对没有领导人的运动持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And then I knew that the killing of Alton Sterling was going to be another flashpoint in the movement.
sentences.zh: 然后我知道，阿尔顿·斯特林的被杀将成为这场运动的又一个引爆点。

sentences.en: Alton Sterling is killed by police in Baton Rouge.
sentences.zh: 阿尔顿·斯特林在巴吞鲁日被警察杀害。

sentences.en: He's the man who was sitting outside a grocery store and selling CDs when someone called the police about a person who had a gun
sentences.zh: 他是那个坐在杂货店外卖CD的人，当时有人报警说有一个人拿着枪，

sentences.en: and the officers who respond to the call end up killing him.
sentences.zh: 而赶到现场的警员最终杀了他。

sentences.en: So when that happens, again, activists from all over the country get in their cars and start heading to Baton Rouge.
sentences.zh: 所以当这件事发生时，全国各地的激进分子再次坐上汽车，开始驶向巴吞鲁日。

sentences.en: A couple of my friends from Ferguson, you know, we get on a call because we always get on a call and we're like, well, what are we going to do?
sentences.zh: 我来自弗格森的几个朋友，你知道的，我们通了电话，因为我们总是会通电话，然后我们就在想，好吧，我们要做什么？

sentences.en: And they're like, we're going to drive down to Baton Rouge.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们要开车去巴吞鲁日。

sentences.en: And I remember being terrified at sending them off to drive through Mississippi and into Louisiana, right?
sentences.zh: 我记得当时吓坏了，因为要送他们开车穿过密西西比州进入路易斯安那州，对吧？

sentences.en: A state whose history I knew well because I'd learned it from my grandparents.
sentences.zh: 那里的历史我很熟悉，因为我是从祖父母那里学来的。

sentences.en: So that fear, Sharonda says, is in the groundwater in Louisiana, which makes going there to protest an entirely different experience and a very scary one for her.
sentences.zh: 夏龙达说，这种恐惧存在于路易斯安那州的地下水中，这使得去那里抗议成为一种完全不同的体验，对她来说非常可怕。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it feels really important.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，这又显得非常重要。

sentences.en: And she just kind of feels like, if I'm going to commit myself to this movement, then, you know, this is, in a way, exactly where I need to be.
sentences.zh: 她只是觉得，如果我要投身于这场运动，那么，你知道的，从某种意义上说，这就是我应该去的地方。

sentences.en: I need to be in uncomfortable places.
sentences.zh: 我需要身处让人感到不适的地方。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so the next day, she packs up her car.
sentences.zh: 于是第二天，她收拾好车子。

sentences.en: She heads to meet her friends in Baton Rouge.
sentences.zh: 她动身去巴吞鲁日与朋友会合。

sentences.en: And what happens once she gets to Baton Rouge?
sentences.zh: 一旦她到达巴吞鲁日，会发生什么？

sentences.en: As soon as the sun sets, the police show up in riot gear and just sort of, they block the street.
sentences.zh: 太阳刚落山，防暴警察就出现了，他们差不多就是直接把街道封锁了。

sentences.en: And you end up in these confrontations with the Baton Rouge Police Department that almost immediately feel like,
sentences.zh: 然后你就会与巴吞鲁日警察局陷入这种对峙，这几乎立刻让你觉得，

sentences.en: you have no plans to let me peacefully proteSt.
sentences.zh: 你们根本不打算让我和平抗议。

sentences.en: You know, the local law enforcement makes clear that they're not happy about people being in the streets.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当地执法部门明确表示，他们对人们走上街头感到很不高兴。

sentences.en: And there are a series of very tense standoffs and a lot of arrests, including one of Sharonda's close friends,
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一系列高度紧张的对峙和大量逮捕，其中包括夏龙达的密友之一，

sentences.en: DeRay McKesson, who basically gets tackled and carted away in handcuffs just as they're walking to their car.
sentences.zh: 德雷·麦克森，他基本上刚走到车旁就被扑倒并戴上手铐带走了。

sentences.en: But that, for us, was a reminder of just how dangerous this work is, right?
sentences.zh: 但对我们来说，那是一个提醒，提醒我们这项工作有多么危险，对吧？

sentences.en: That even if you are not physically positioning yourself as the leader, any one of us can be arrested, right, at any time.
sentences.zh: 那就是，即使你没有把自己定位为领导者，我们中的任何一个人也随时可能被捕，对吧？

sentences.en: And sometimes that's the best case scenario.
sentences.zh: 有时那是最好的情况。

sentences.en: And I remember, you know, checking in with myself and asking, like, are you courageous enough to do this?
sentences.zh: 我记得，你知道的，我审视了自己并问道，你是否有勇气做这件事？

sentences.en: And I think that doing that in high school, I go back to that moment a lot.
sentences.zh: 我想在高中时这样做过，我经常回想起那个时刻。

sentences.en: And often when I am protesting and when I am showing up, I am showing up for that girl.
sentences.zh: 通常当我参与抗议和现身时，我是为了那个女孩而现身的。

sentences.en: So, at this point, it's two years into the movement and the country is really paying attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，此时此刻，这场运动已经进行两年了，全国上下都在高度关注。

sentences.en: The president is paying attention.
sentences.zh: 总统在关注。

sentences.en: And the 2016 election is right around the corner.
sentences.zh: 2016年大选也近在咫尺。

sentences.en: So, we were all gearing up to fight Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们都在摩拳擦掌准备对抗希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: We were all gearing up to say we want to build on the momentum that we have built.
sentences.zh: 我们都在摩拳擦掌地表示，我们要巩固已经建立的势头。

sentences.en: And then we got Trump.
sentences.zh: 然后我们迎来了特朗普。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, everybody.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: And as soon as he takes office, it's as if the entire progressive policy platform is under siege.
sentences.zh: 他一上任，整个进步派的政策纲领就仿佛遭到了围攻。

sentences.en: Overnight, another surge of protests against President Trump's controversial executive order.
sentences.zh: 一夜之间，又掀起了一波抗议浪潮，反对特朗普总统极具争议的行政命令。

sentences.en: A new initiative that would separate children from their parents if they tried to enter the United States illegally.
sentences.zh: 一项新举措：如果试图非法进入美国，将把儿童与其父母骨肉分离。

sentences.en: With protesters storming major cities all across the country.
sentences.zh: 抗议者涌入全国各大城市。

sentences.en: Outraged after the Trump administration announced it's rescinding DACA, giving Congress six months to come up.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普政府宣布废除DACA、给国会六个月时间提出方案后，人们愤怒不已。

sentences.en: They're calling this the largest youth-led protest since the Vietnam War era.
sentences.zh: 他们称这是自越南战争时代以来规模最大的青年领导的抗议活动。

sentences.en: But these young activists are taking a stand in a country that is deeply divided over guns.
sentences.zh: 但这些年轻的活动人士在一个对枪支问题深度分裂的国家中采取了立场。

sentences.en: The issues seemed so much bigger and of so much greater immediate importance.
sentences.zh: 这些问题看起来要大得多，而且具有更重大的迫切重要性。

sentences.en: And I don't even know how I can bring myself to say that, knowing that the issues we were organizing around were literally issues of life and death.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道自己怎么能说出这话，因为我知道我们所组织的抗议活动简直就是生死攸关的问题。

sentences.en: But we start to see the dehumanizing of entire communities.
sentences.zh: 但我们开始看到整个社区被去人性化。

sentences.en: And policing just sort of got bumped down the list of priorities.
sentences.zh: 而警务问题在优先级列表中被挤下去了。

sentences.en: And some folks show up with their Black Lives Matter gear or their signs.
sentences.zh: 有些人带着“黑人的命也是命”的装备或标语出现。

sentences.en: But there is a sense that it had become one of many sets of demands.
sentences.zh: 但有一种感觉是，它已经沦为众多诉求中的一个。

sentences.en: This idea of Black Lives Matter really fades into the background.
sentences.zh: “黑人的命也是命”这种理念真的淡出了背景。

sentences.en: And we just, we didn't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们，我们就不再谈论它了。

sentences.en: You know, the interesting thing is you had asked me earlier what it felt like post-92.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有趣的是，你之前问过我92年之后是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And that's what it felt like.
sentences.zh: 那就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: One day it was my entire world.
sentences.zh: 有一天，它还是我的整个世界。

sentences.en: And the next day no one talked about it.
sentences.zh: 而第二天，就没有人再谈论它了。

sentences.en: Did that feel like a failure?
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是一次失败吗？

sentences.en: When all the momentum disappeared and fell flat?
sentences.zh: 当所有的势头都消失并归于平静时？

sentences.en: In our quiet moments, some of us reflect on the trauma we experienced.
sentences.zh: 在安静的时刻，我们中的一些人会反思我们经历的心灵创伤。

sentences.en: Some of us reflect on the sacrifices we made, right, to jobs, to credit scores, to savings accounts.
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人会反思我们做出的牺牲，对吧，对工作、对信用评分、对储蓄账户的牺牲。

sentences.en: And we do ask ourselves if it was worth it.
sentences.zh: 我们会问自己这一切是否值得。

sentences.en: Do you have any regrets from that time?
sentences.zh: 你对那段时期有什么遗憾吗？

sentences.en: I wish you did anything differently.
sentences.zh: 我希望你当时做过什么不同的事。

sentences.en: That's a really hard question to answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难回答的问题。

sentences.en: I wish we had done a better job of talking about the importance of both inside the system activism and outside the system activism.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们当时能做得更好，讨论体制内活动和体制外活动两者都很重要的意义。

sentences.en: And by that I mean it took us a couple of years to get to the point where many of us felt we could do things like run for office.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们花了几年时间才走到这一步，当时我们中的许多人觉得我们可以做一些事情，比如竞选公职。

sentences.en: And not feel like sellouts, not feel like our only credibility came from being in the streets.
sentences.zh: 并且不觉得自己是卖国贼，不觉得我们唯一的信誉来自于走上街头。

sentences.en: And I wish we had gotten there sooner.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能早点走到这一步。

sentences.en: I think we could have helped usher in a new wave of leadership much earlier.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们本可以更早地协助开启新一波领导层。

sentences.en: We could have pushed to have our people in places of real decision-making power.
sentences.zh: 我们本可以推动让我们的自己人进入真正拥有决策权的职位。

sentences.en: And I wish I wish I hadn't been naive.
sentences.zh: 我希望，我希望自己当初没有那么天真。

sentences.en: And I wish that I had been just a little more realistic about how long change actually takes.
sentences.zh: 我希望自己当时能对变革实际需要多长时间有更现实一点的认识。

sentences.en: I will say I didn't think we'd be back here this soon.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我没想到我们会这么快又回到这里。

sentences.en: You've been here before.
sentences.zh: 你以前来过这里。

sentences.en: So is there anything right now that you're afraid of?
sentences.zh: 那么现在有什么让你感到害怕的事吗？

sentences.en: I'm afraid of my country and my countrymen breaking my heart again.
sentences.zh: 我害怕我的国家和我的同胞再次伤我的心。

sentences.en: I am afraid that we are going to take very shallow and superficial signals of allyship as a sign of real change.
sentences.zh: 我害怕我们将把肤浅和表面的同盟姿态当作真正改变的标志。

sentences.en: And I don't know if we have done the work of helping people imagine what the future can look like.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们是否做了应做的工作来帮助人们想象未来会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And I think that's the next phase of the work.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是下一步的工作。

sentences.en: We have gotten people to a point where they know that something has to fundamentally change, that we can no longer tinker around the edges.
sentences.zh: 我们已经让人们认识到，有些事情必须发生根本性的改变，我们不能再小修小补了。

sentences.en: But I don't know if we've helped them imagine what we have to build in its place.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道我们是否帮他们想象了我们必须在废墟上建立什么。

sentences.en: Are you hopeful now that change is coming?
sentences.zh: 你现在对变革即将到来抱有希望吗？

sentences.en: Am I hopeful now that change is coming?
sentences.zh: 我对变革即将到来抱有希望吗？

sentences.en: I have to be.
sentences.zh: 我必须有。

sentences.en: If I was not hopeful that change was coming, I would not be in the streets.
sentences.zh: 如果我对变革的到来不抱希望，我就不会走上街头。

sentences.en: If I was not hopeful that change was coming, there would be no point in having this conversation.
sentences.zh: 如果我对变革的到来不抱希望，进行这场对话也就毫无意义了。

sentences.en: You know, hope is really important in this work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这项工作中，希望真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And you have to hope that tomorrow can be better than today.
sentences.zh: 你必须心怀希望，相信明天会比今天更好。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it makes showing up impossible.
sentences.zh: 否则，现身就成了不可能的事。

sentences.en: Black Lives Matter.
sentences.zh: 黑人的命也是命。

sentences.en: I got chills.
sentences.zh: 我起鸡皮疙瘩了。

sentences.en: This looks so good.
sentences.zh: 这看起来太棒了。

sentences.en: I wonder what Sharonda thinks her grandmother would make of the decisions that she has made and of the life that she is now leading and the role she's playing in this movement.
sentences.zh: 我想知道夏龙达认为她的祖母会对她所做出的决定、她现在过的生活以及她在运动中扮演的角色作何感想。

sentences.en: She does think back about her grandmother a lot, and she wonders if this is the life her grandmother envisioned for her.
sentences.zh: 她确实经常回想起祖母，并且想知道这是否是她祖母为她设想的人生。

sentences.en: Is there something you would ask her if you could?
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，有什么事是你想问她的吗？

sentences.en: If I could ask my grandmother something, what would I ask her?
sentences.zh: 如果我可以问祖母一件事，我会问她什么？

sentences.en: You know, given my grandmother's personality, I think I would say, or ask her,
sentences.zh: 鉴于我祖母的个性，我想我会说，或者问她，

sentences.en: if she knew it would turn out like this for me.
sentences.zh: 如果她知道我的人生会变成这样。

sentences.en: My hunch is, she probably hoped it did.
sentences.zh: 我的直觉是，她可能希望它是这样的。

sentences.en: I could have chosen to do anything other than this.
sentences.zh: 我本可以选择做别的事情，而不是这个。

sentences.en: But my sense is my grandmother probably knew that I was always going to be this person.
sentences.zh: 但我的直觉是，我祖母可能知道我注定会成为这样一个人。

sentences.en: I would want to ask her that.
sentences.zh: 我很想问她那个问题。

sentences.en: The protests aren't getting as much coverage.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动的报道没有那么多了。

sentences.en: The crowds are still big.
sentences.zh: 人群依然庞大。

sentences.en: At least the ones I've seen.
sentences.zh: 至少我看到的那些是这样。

sentences.en: Not as big as a couple weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 没有几周前那么大。

sentences.en: Not as big as some of the daytime marches and rallies.
sentences.zh: 没有一些日间游行和集会那么大。

sentences.en: But definitely bigger than they have been in a long while.
